it now applies only to a bare push with no refspec (the destination-ref
check is authoritative for any push with an explicit destination), and
it checks BOTH the payload cwd and the invocation's own resolved -C/cd

scope only ever broadens denial, never narrows it. This flips two
existing test expectations (documented in no-push-to-main_test.sh):
pushing a feature branch while cwd is on main is now allowed (the
destination governs, not cwd), and a bare push via a relative cd to a
feature worktree is now denied when cwd itself is on main (scope no
longer silently overrides a cwd that is itself unsafe).

All 46 existing cases pass under the updated expectations.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <[redacted-email]>
EOF
)"

tool_input.new_string:
# run_hook PATH_OVERRIDE PAYLOAD_FILE PROJECT_DIR -- invokes the hook with a
# given PATH (real or the no-jq allowlist) and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. Prints
# the hook's stdout followed by a line "EXIT_STATUS=<n>" so the caller can
# tell a crashed hook (non-zero exit) from a clean allow (exit 0, empty
# stdout) -- a crashed hook must never be read as an allow just because it
# produced no deny payload.
run_hook() {
    local path_override="$1" payload_file="$2" project_dir="$3"
    local output status
    output=$(PATH="$path_override" CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$project_dir" bash "$HOOK" <"$payload_file")
    status=$?
    printf '%s' "$output"
    printf '\nEXIT_STATUS=%d\n' "$status"
}

# assert_decision DESC PATH_LABEL PATH_OVERRIDE COMMAND CWD PROJECT_DIR WANT
# WANT is "deny" or "allow". Builds the payload, runs the hook, and checks:
# exit status is 0; for "allow", stdout is exactly empty; for "deny",
# stdout is exactly one JSON line whose permissionDecision is "deny". A
# non-zero exit status fails the case outright, regardless of what (if
# anything) the hook printed -- a crashed hook must never be read as an
# allow.
assert_decision() {
    local desc="$1" path_label="$2" path_override="$3" command="$4" cwd="$5" \
        project_dir="$6" want="$7"
    CASES=$((CASES + 1))

    local payload_file
    payload_file=$(mktemp)
    json_payload "$command" "$cwd" >"$payload_file"

    local raw status output
    raw=$(run_hook "$path_override" "$payload_file" "$project_dir")
    rm -f "$payload_file"

    status=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | sed -n 's/^EXIT_STATUS=\([0-9]*\)$/\1/p' | tail -1)
    output=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | sed '$d')

    local fail_reason=""
    if [[ "$status" != "0" ]]; then
        fail_reason="hook exited non-zero ($status) -- treated as a crash, not an allow"
    elif [[ "$want" == "allow" ]]; then
        if [[ -n "$output" ]]; then
            fail_reason="want=allow requires exactly empty stdout"
        fi
    else
        local line_count
        line_count=$(printf '%s\n' "$output" | grep -c '.')
        if [[ "$line_count" -ne 1 ]]; then
            fail_reason="want=deny requires exactly one output line, got $line_count"
        elif ! printf '%s' "$output" | grep -q '"permissionDecision":"deny"'; then
            fail_reason="want=deny but output has no permissionDecision:deny"
        fi
    fi

    if [[ -z "$fail_reason" ]]; then
        printf 'PASS [%s] %s\n' "$path_label" "$desc"
    else
        printf 'FAIL [%s] %s: want=%s status=%s reason=%s output=%s\n' \
            "$path_label" "$desc" "$want" "$status" "$fail_reason" "$output"
        FAILURES=$((FAILURES + 1))
